messages:
mike: Noticing a regression after the kernel-selector tweak yesterday. Longer sequences (2k+) occasionally produce NaNs in attention logits when using ROPE+ALiBi mix. Root cause unclear, assigning brainstorming here.

tara: Seen this locally too. Small percentage of requests only; looks like it correlates with fp16->bf16 fastpath on Ampere builds. :grimacing:

sanjay: Can you paste a minimal stack trace / failing op? Might be accumulation overflow in the rotary application or exp() blowing up.

mike: Minimal snippet from logs:
```
RuntimeError: attention_scores contains NaN
  at attn_forward (kernels/attn.cu:842)
  kernel: rope_alibi_mix_fastpath
```

elaine: Hypothesis: kernel selector picked an optimized kernel that trades extra accumulator headroom for throughput, reducing internal eps clamps. When combined with ALiBi slope scaling at long distances we get large positive logits -> exp overflow -> NaN.

jess: Agreed. We saw similar when we removed the eps guard in posenc kernels during last perf patch. Suggest adding a cheap clamp/guard around the exp and in the softmax numerator path.

mike: Quick test patch recommended by jess:
```
// ensure finite logits before softmax
logits = min(logits, 1e4f);
logits = max(logits, -1e4f);
// fallback guard
if (!isfinite(sum(exp(logits)))) logits = logits * 0.1f;
```

tara: That guard is OK for a hotfix, but we need to understand why the optimized kernel loses headroom. Maybe accumulators are narrower (bf16 multiply accumulate) vs reference fp32 path. Sanjay, any telemetry on accumulator dtype per kernel variant?

sanjay: Yep. Kernel selector map: fastpath uses bf16 accum with fused matmul+scale, fallback uses fp32 accum. Telemetry shows ~2.1% of requests picked the fastpath on that build/date. I'll dump the selector table and recent rollouts.

infra-bot: deploy-rollout: kernel-selector:v2 rolled to 25% @ 1972223200 by ci/canary

elaine: That explains the partial nature. We should revert the selector for the canary and add unit tests for large sequence ALiBi + ROPE combos.

mike: Action items:
- sanjay: revert canary to v1 for the region (urgent) [ETA 30m]
- jess: land a defensive clamp hotfix in the optimized kernel (small perf cost) [ETA 2h]
- tara: add regression test (seq_len=2048, alibi_slope=high, bf16 path) to CI [ETA EOD]
- elaine: run numeric stress harness across quant levels (fp32, bf16, int8 emulate) [ETA tomorrow]

sanjay: Starting revert now.

jess: I'll open PR for clamp, will include perf measurement. If perf drop >4% we may instead add selective clamp based on max(|logits|) detection.

mike: Good. Also consider KV-cache alignment effect — if caching shifts index offsets, ALiBi slope multiplies larger distance than expected. Could interact. Anyone seen cache-index offsets in recent patch?

tara: We did a small cache refactor last week but added unit tests that passed. Still worth an audit.

elaine: Note for long-term: we should unify kernel ABI to advertise accumulator dtype and numeric guards. Kernel selector should not pick a variant that weakens numeric invariants without an explicit opt-in.

jess: Agreed. RFC idea: kernel capability flags: {accum_dtype, has_eps_guard, max_logit_abs}. Selector consults required_flags from operator config. That avoids accidental regressions.

mike: Perfect. For now do the revert + hotfix. Keep thread updates small. Ping me when revert done.

infra-bot: deploy-status: canary-revert for kernel-selector:v1 started @ 1972223600

sanjay: Revert completed, confirmed 100% traffic on v1 in that region. Monitoring for NaNs ongoing.

tara: After revert, NaN volume dropped to baseline. Hotfix PR from jess looks good, running perf bench now.

jess: Perf: clamp-only patch adds ~0.9% p99 latency on our synthetic long-seq workload, token throughput -0.6%. I'll include selective threshold variant in PR.

mike: Thanks. We'll fast-track hotfix and schedule the RFC for capability flags. Closing this thread when RFC draft exists. :thumbsup:

elaine: Filing follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-1147 "kernel capability flags + selector safety". Adding owners: ela, jess, sanjay.

mike: Thanks everyone. If you see any new NaN spikes, call pager immediately.
